decisions.reason: As a broad supplement line closely related to the firm's existing consumer-health and pharmacy business, it fits the firm's knowledge base well and a large R&D-active pharma firm would usually refine rather than withdraw it after several years of learning.

This skin-and-hair supplement remains close to the firm's established OTC capabilities, so the firm can absorb market feedback through existing development, quality, and pharmacy-channel know-how and is more likely to keep it.

Although less prominently signaled than the broader supplement line, the joint-health product still builds on related consumer-health knowledge and can be improved with limited additional learning, making continuation more likely than exit.

The generic blood-pressure medicine had an early problem signal, but by 2022 the firm's strong regulatory, analytical, and manufacturing capabilities imply that it has had time to assimilate the issue and commercialize corrective learning, so keeping it is still more likely.

The OTC migraine triptan is somewhat less aligned with the firm's established supplement expansion path, but it still draws on the firm's pharmaceutical development, regulatory, and pharmacy-market capabilities, so management would tend to continue it while monitoring performance closely.
